record.paper_title: 20 Open Questions About Deformations of Compactifiable Manifolds
record.original_question: The paper introduces two notions of deformation for connected complex manifolds in the noncompact setting. One is a C-infinity map f: X -> Y whose fibers are connected complex n-manifolds given by local fiberwise complex coordinates, without assuming properness or C-infinity local triviality. The other is a holomorphic surjective submersion π: X~ -> D over a complex disc with central fiber X that is locally trivial in the C-infinity category. Under what hypotheses are these two notions equivalent, or when does one imply the other?

evidence.quote: Remark 7. Note that in Def. 3 we are not assuming that f is locally trivial in the C∞-category. Def. 3 is not the same that [GR, Def. 9].
Question 1. Under what conditions we can say that the two notions of deformations mentioned above are equivalent, or one implies the other?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider connected complex manifolds in the noncompact setting, and the following two notions of a deformation of a connected complex n-manifold X:

(A) A C^∞ map f : 𝒳 → Y between C^∞ manifolds, with Y connected, such that there exists a distinguished point 0 ∈ Y with f^{-1}(0) biholomorphic to X, and such that each fiber X_y := f^{-1}(y) carries the structure of a connected complex n-manifold induced by a system of local "fiberwise complex coordinates" on 𝒳: that is, each point of 𝒳 has an open neighborhood U with C^∞ coordinates (z_1,…,z_n, t_1,…,t_m) such that (t_1,…,t_m) are pulled back from C^∞ coordinates on Y and (z_1,…,z_n) restrict to holomorphic coordinates on each fiber. No properness of f and no C^∞ local triviality of f are assumed.

(B) A holomorphic surjective submersion π : 𝒳̃ → D, where D ⊂ ℂ is an open disc centered at 0, such that π^{-1}(0) is biholomorphic to X and π is locally trivial in the C^∞ category (i.e. for every point of D there exists an open neighborhood V ⊂ D and a C^∞ diffeomorphism π^{-1}(V) ≅ V × X over V).

Determine hypotheses on X, on the base, and/or on the map under which a deformation in sense (A) gives rise to a deformation in sense (B), and conversely. In particular, identify natural sufficient conditions under which the two notions coincide.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as one of a list of open questions about deformations of compactifiable noncompact complex manifolds. No subsequent work resolving the equivalence of these two notions of deformation in the noncompact / non-proper setting was found in available sources; related results address only special cases (e.g. asymptotically cylindrical Calabi–Yau manifolds, tame deformations of Stein manifolds).

status_evidence.title: 20 open questions about deformations of compactifiable manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Paper provides a list of open questions intended as a guide for further research on deformations in the noncompact setting.
status_evidence.claim: The equivalence of the two deformation notions is listed as an open question.

status_evidence.title: The Moduli Space of Asymptotically Cylindrical Calabi–Yau Manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Deformation theory of asymptotically cylindrical Calabi–Yau manifolds is unobstructed.
status_evidence.claim: Related results exist only in special compactifiable settings, not addressing the general equivalence.

status_evidence.title: Deformations of Open Stein Manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Tame, compactly-supported deformations of a Stein manifold are trivial.
status_evidence.claim: Related noncompact deformation results are restricted to tame/Stein settings.
